content: When authoring a commit message that documents what a commit-msg hook rejects, don't reproduce the offending pattern verbatim in the body — the hook will match it and block the commit that ships the hook. Reference the file (e.g. "see .githooks/commit-msg for the full list") or paraphrase the pattern so it doesn't literally match.
context: While flattening this session's work into one PR commit, the flatten commit itself was blocked by the newly-installed commit-msg hook because the commit body listed the trailer patterns the hook rejects (including `claude.ai/code/session_`). That literal string matched the hook's own regex. Nice proof-of-work that the hook is doing its job, but a genuine friction the second time around. Fix was to rewrite the message to reference the hook file rather than reproducing the pattern. Landed as commit b5f65d2 on branch chore/paper-cuts (PR #12).
title: A commit-msg pattern hook fires on messages that describe the pattern
